newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI may cap rupee, allow money supply rise.
newsitem.headline: India RBI may cap rupee, allow money supply rise.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is likely to keep a strong rupee on a tight leash and allow money supply to grow, an economist said on Wednesday.

"Probably they (the RBI) will have money supply growth .. rather than allow the rupee to rise because export markets have been quite sluggish and they are concerned about that," Sanjeev Sanyal, economist at Soc-Gen Crosby India told Reuters Financial Television.
"We do not expect the rupee to appreciate too much but definitely remain at this level," he said.
The rupee was trading at seven-month highs of 35.70 to a dollar on Wednesday helped by strong foreign inflows.

He said the central bank had been fighting a battle on two fronts -- by buying up rising dollar inflows to keep the rupee from appreciating, and controlling domestic money supply growth by heavy borrowings.
The RBI has already raised nearly 60 percent of the borrowings programme for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), and it would have reached its target by September, he said.
"It will find that it will either have to let the currency appreciate or it will have to allow money supply rise very sharply," Sanyal said.
The Indian economy which was suffering from a demand problem and huge overcapacity may come to the RBI's rescue, he said.
"They might feel that excess money supply will feed into production rather than inflation," he said. "So, given the choice that might be the best option."

Sanyal said the upward pressure on the rupee would continue for at least seven months because of planned government plans to divest holdings in state-run firms through global depositary receipts issues.
One such issue by Gas Authority of India Ltd would alone bring in about $800 million, he said.
Over the longer term the rupee would depreciate, he said.
"Looking further out I think the rupee in real exchange rate terms is about 7-8 percent overvalued," he said.
"In the longer run it will probably have to depreciate keeping in mind that all its competitors are depreciating at this moment of time in South Asia," he added.
